title: Lior and the Signal
premise: Vesper Oyelaran, navigator of the hauler Lior, has spent years ferrying supplies past Kestrel's Landing, a colony that went dark during the war and whose cryo-backups sleep forgotten in the hold. When gravity stutters across the system for nine seconds, the Lior is thrown into the colony's orbit — where Vesper discovers survivors who have been broadcasting a peace signal no one will hear. The message carries proof that both governments manufactured the war to seize the colony's memory-harvesting technology, and delivering it means betraying Vesper's own fleet family. In the end, Vesper chooses the dead over the living powers, transmitting the truth at the cost of the Lior itself, and the surviving colonists — the found family Vesper never expected — scatter into the dark carrying copies of the signal.
about_author: Quentin Underhill is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who keep records no one asked for.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A routine supply run past the silent colony world when gravity fails for exactly nine seconds, hurling the Lior off-course. Vesper logs the anomaly obsessively, as they log everything, while the crew argues about turning back. Emotional beat: unease — the universe has hiccupped, and Vesper alone writes it down.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with interludes from the ship's aging AI, Mother Corvid. We learn what haunts Vesper: two hundred cryo-backups of Kestrel's Landing colonists, legally abandoned, riding in the hold for six years. The flicker has woken one pod. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh — someone is breathing again because Vesper didn't let go.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Landing Still Answers
chapters.summary: The awakened colonist, an engineer named Iyo Sefu, reveals the colony survived underground — and has been broadcasting a peace signal for years on a band everyone stopped monitoring. Vesper's POV. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery; the dead were never dead.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Taught Me to Forget
chapters.summary: Fleet orders arrive: investigate the anomaly, then scuttle any unauthorized transmissions. Vesper realizes command already knows about the signal and has been suppressing it. POV shifts to Captain Adeyemi, torn between loyalty and conscience. Emotional beat: the first crack in Vesper's faith in their found family aboard the Lior.

chapters.title: Descent into the Green Dark
chapters.summary: Vesper and Iyo land on Kestrel's Landing, walking through overgrown ruins into the living colony beneath. Vesper's POV. The colonists show them the memory-harvest: technology that stores human experience — the true prize both governments want. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror at what the war was really for.

chapters.title: The Archive Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Inside the archive, Vesper touches harvested memories — including their own childhood, recorded without consent by the colony's early census program. Vesper's POV. The message they must deliver becomes personal: it contains proof the war was engineered, plus every stolen memory. Emotional beat: violation and recognition; memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Orders to Burn
chapters.summary: Captain Adeyemi's POV. The fleet orders the Lior to destroy the colony's transmitter and jettison the backups as biohazard. Adeyemi must choose between her crew's survival and her conscience; she quietly gives Vesper a window to act and deniability. Emotional beat: love expressed as betrayal of duty.

chapters.title: Every Hand Against the Signal
chapters.summary: Both fleets converge on Kestrel's Landing as the nine-second flicker repeats — the colony's harvest array straining against something vast. Vesper races to boost the transmitter through the interference while crewmates defect or resist. Rising action peaks. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; time running out measured in seconds.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Vesper merges with the archive to amplify the signal, sacrificing their own stored memories as fuel, while the Lior rams the jamming relay above. The truth floods every receiver in the system: the war's origin, the stolen memories, the sleeping names read aloud. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure — giving memory away to save it.

chapters.title: Copies in the Dark
chapters.summary: Resolution. The war stalls as the broadcast spreads; the fleets fracture under public reckoning. Iyo and the colonists disperse with duplicated archives, promising to find each other again. Vesper, memory-thinned but alive, keeps a single recording: the crew of the Lior laughing. Emotional beat: grief braided with hope — found family persists even when memory doesn't.
